facts.text: More than 30 per cent of Penticton's population is 65 years and older, according to the 2021 Census.

facts.text: Penticton's two largest industries are tourism and the growing wine industry.

facts.text: Over 2,000 people work in tourism-related businesses in Penticton, about 11 percent of the workforce.
facts.evidence: Over 2,000 people are currently employed in tourism-related businesses in Penticton, representing about 11 percent of the workforce

facts.text: Penticton has been named the eighth most livable medium-sized city in Canada.
facts.evidence: Penticton named #8 most livable medium-sized city in Canada

meta.descriptor: a lakeside city in British Columbia's South Okanagan
meta.fact: a tourism and wine-industry hub where over 2,000 people work in tourism-related businesses

overview: Penticton had 36,885 residents in the 2021 Census, up 9.3 percent from 33,761 in 2016, in 17,361 occupied homes on 43.03 square kilometres. Seniors make up a large share of residents, so many customers value trusted local providers, clear information and personal service.
Tourism and the wine industry lead the economy, bringing seasonal visitors who add to summer demand for food, lodging and services.

byService.lead-generation: Penticton lead generation should run two tracks: steady, trust-based outreach to an older resident base and seasonal campaigns aimed at summer visitors drawn by lakes and wineries.
byService.seo: Search plans for Penticton should cover tourism queries about wineries, beaches and lodging, plus local service terms residents use, since both audiences search for the city by name.
byService.website-development: Because seniors make up a large share of Penticton customers, websites should use large readable text, plain navigation and visible phone numbers, while staying fast on mobile for visitors.
byService.branding: Penticton branding can draw on the lakes, vineyards and relaxed South Okanagan pace, but should stay warm and dependable for long-term residents rather than purely touristic.
